chapter: Home life and the father's death
title: Father leaves for Bay St. Louis to escape rising segregation
summary: Tio says his father moved the family to Bay St. Louis because segregation was beginning in New Orleans, and he wrote to the Mexican consul about returning to Mexico before falling ill.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Do you know if your father and uncle ever went back to Mexico to visit any relatives? Did you ever hear them say if they were going back to visit anyone? Well, I want to be frank with you.

You see, my father when he was living, he came down here. And the reason why we went to Bay St. Louis, I'm going to tell you. People here had a nice way of living. And like I told you, my father used to play with different bands. They were one. They were white and Negro. They made no difference in the relation. They were in the color as long as you were able to do something. That was the time in them days. Well, after this became the coming, my father then decided that he seemed to change. How did people begin to segregate?
Yeah, the prejudice and segregation came in after his lifetime.

So he told my mother, this is no place for us to raise our children. We got to get out of here. Well, he went to Bay St. Louis. Well, in Bay St. Louis everything was pretty cheap. You had house rent was cheaper. They had work. Then he had his music. He had his people just to send him orchestration to write from all parts of the city and different bands. He made money at it. He told my mother that he was going to write to the Mexican council, which he did. He had written to him and he told him that he wanted to come back to Mexico. Well, the council sent him a letter back. But he was, my father had taken sick. We moved from Bay St. Louis back here. Then the letter came in from Mexico. Told him to bring in all his, get all his papers set up to get him, bring him back. Come on back to Mexico and transportation and be paid. Then he, had he lived we wouldn't have been here.
